100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On September 15, 1926, the world witnessed significant political shifts as the British Parliament debated the controversial Joseph Chamberlain's plan for tariff reform, stirring public opinion across the nation. In the United States, President Calvin Coolidge addressed the growing concerns over agricultural distress, emphasizing the need for federal assistance to farmers. Meanwhile, a major earthquake struck the city of Managua, Nicaragua, causing widespread destruction and prompting international relief efforts.
